{{Quote|A Jedi is not proud or boastful, and I trust you will understand I am sincere when I say that it is hard for me to imagine that the guard might have spied me in the first place, had I not wished to be seen.|Master Poof lectures on his abilities to bend the perceptions of others|<ref name="JVS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
'''Yarael Poof''' was a wise [[Quermian/Legends|Quermian]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and [[Jedi Consular]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quermia/Legends|Quermia]] who was a member of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] by [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]]. He was legendary for his skills at [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trickery]], and he was the senior-most of four Quermian [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. He was the master of Jedi Master [[Roron Corobb/Legends|Roron Corobb]]. Poof was held in respect for his insight and was skilled with the ability of [[battle meditation]]&mdash;which had proven instrumental in bringing about the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] victory during the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] in 44 BBY. In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], Poof was present in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and aided in defending it from a [[Raid on the Jedi Temple (Yinchorri Uprising)|raid]] conducted by [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]] forces during the [[Yinchorri Uprising]]. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Poof was among the Council as they investigated a string of incidents that targeted [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] of the Republic.

Later in 32 BBY, Poof was present for the initial testing of the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], and he was among the High Council when they denied Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn's]] request to [[Jedi training/Legends|train]] the boy. However, the Council reversed their decision following Jinn's [[Death/Legends|death]] and granted the newly anointed [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]&mdash;and Jinn's own [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] until his death&mdash;[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] permission to train Skywalker. In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], Poof took it upon himself to look into the potential presence of the [[Infant of Shaa]], an ancient artifact that was capable of rending an entire planet apart through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], on Coruscant. Poof's investigation led him deep into Coruscant, where he encountered the radical [[General/Legends|General]] [[Ashaar Khorda]] attempting to use the artifact to destroy Coruscant. Poof was mortally wounded by Khorda but managed to deactivate the Infant of Shaa in his final moments, saving the planet from destruction. Following his death, he was replaced on the High Council by Jedi Master [[Coleman Trebor/Legends|Coleman Trebor]].

==Biography==
===On the Jedi Council===
{{Quote|Before you can bring these planets together to talk you will need to assess the matter carefully. There may be more at stake here than meets the eye.|Yarael Poof, to Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ThreatWithin">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Threat Within]]''</ref>}}
[[File:SW39CarrierYoungling.png|thumb|right|250px|The Jedi High Council, Poof included, communicates with Plo Koon through Sha Koon.]]
Yarael Poof was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Quermian/Legends|Quermian]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and [[Jedi Consular]]<ref name="PowerOfTheJedi" /> hailing from<ref name="YaraelDB" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quermia/Legends|Quermia]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> By [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]],<ref name="SW39Date">[[Star Wars (1998) 36|''Star Wars'' (1998) 36]] dates itself to thirty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the events of {{Film|IV}}, which are dated by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. As such, ''Star Wars'' 36 takes place in [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]]. The issue also states the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] took place fourteen years ago, corresponding to [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]]. As [[Star Wars (1998) 39|''Star Wars'' (1998) 39]] continues the same recounting of the Stark Hyperspace War, the flashbacks in that issue must also take place in 44 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].</ref> Poof was a member of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] within the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]],<ref name="SW-1998-39">[[Star Wars (1998) 39|''Star Wars'' (1998) 39]]</ref> having accepted an invitation to join it<ref name="FactFile100" /> and serving a lifetime term.<ref name="CSWEJediCouncil">{{CSWECite|II|147|Jedi Council}}</ref> He eventually constructed his own [[Yarael Poof's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]<ref name="PowerOfTheJedi" /> and trained his own [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Roron Corobb/Legends|Roron Corobb]].<ref name="CSWERoronCorobb" /> At one point, Poof made a recording in a [[Asli Krimsan's holocron|holocron]] created by Jedi Master [[Asli Krimsan]] in which he gave a lecture on the applications of illusions cast through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. In the lecture, Poof gave his students a hypothetical to consider, wherein they are caught by a guard while infiltrating a secure building and have to utilize illusions to escape. The Quermian Jedi Master provided a variety of potential solutions to the dilemma while also pointing out the potential drawbacks and consequences of each one. Poof advised caution to his students, urging them to consider the repercussions their chosen course of action could have on the hypothetical guard's life. At the end of his lecture, he maintained that while a Jedi was neither proud nor boastful, he found it unlikely that he himself would have been caught in such a situation.<ref name="JediVsSith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

In 44 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="SW39Date" /> the Jedi Order became involved in a conflict with the [[Stark Commercial Combine]] criminal organization: the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]]. During the conflict, Poof was among the High Council members gathered in the [[Jedi Council Chamber/Legends|Jedi Council Chamber]] of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on<ref name="SW-1998-39" /> the planet<ref name="The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as Jedi Master [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] reported to them the circumstances of Jedi Master [[Tyvokka/Legends|Tyvokka's]] [[Death/Legends|death]] on the planet [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]]. As the conflict continued, Poof and the remainder of the Council used the niece of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], [[Sha Koon]], as a conduit to communicate with Plo as he was still on Troiken during the war. This allowed the Council to collaborate with Plo on a plan to send [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] reinforcements to Troiken by brokering an agreement with the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].<ref name="SW-1998-39" /> Poof also used [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]] during the conflict, helping to ensure victory for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TNEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> It was ultimately Plo and the Council's plan that allowed them to bring the war to an end.<ref name="SW-1998-39" />

At some point between 44 and [[37 BBY/Legends|37 BBY]],<ref name="YaddleDate">"[[Yaddle's Tale: The One Below]]" takes place after [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon's]] ascension to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], and prior to [[Yaddle/Legends|Yaddle's]] ascension to the Council. Yaddle appears as a member of the Jedi High Council during [[Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell 1|''Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan: Last Stand on Ord Mantell'' 1]], established in its introduction to take place five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to {{Film|I}}, which is dated by ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], five years after [[37 BBY/Legends|37 BBY]]. Therefore, this story must take place between 44 and 37 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].</ref> Poof&mdash;alongside the other members of the High Council&mdash;convened within the Jedi Council Chamber of the Jedi Temple to discuss the potential of ascending Padawan [[Yaddle/Legends|Yaddle]] to knighthood. After hearing the story of her [[Time/Legends|time]] on the planet [[Koba]], Poof and the rest of the Council agreed to ascend Yaddle not only to knighthood but to the rank of Jedi Master.<ref name="YaddlesTale">"[[Yaddle's Tale: The One Below]]" &ndash; [[Star Wars Tales 5|''Star Wars Tales'' 5]]</ref> In [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]],<ref name="ThreatWithinDate">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Threat Within]]'' to [[40 BBY/Legends|40 BBY]].</ref> the Jedi Council assigned Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his Padawan, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to a [[Mission to Vorzyd IV|mission]] to the planet [[Vorzyd IV]], where they were to investigate a recent string of sabotages the native [[Vorzydiak]] [[Species/Legends|species]] blamed on the neighboring planet of [[Vorzyd V/Legends|Vorzyd V]]. As the Council administered this task on the two Jedi, Poof advised caution, stating that there could be more at stake than it appeared.<ref name="ThreatWithin" /> A [[Standard year/Legends|year]] later, in [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]],<ref name="TheFollowersDate">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the initial events of ''[[Jedi Apprentice Special Edition: The Followers]]'' to [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]].</ref> Kenobi likened the appearance of Quermian [[Professor/Legends|professor]] [[Murk Lundi]] to that of Yarael Poof&mdash;in particular his species and what Kenobi regarded as a commanding presence. As Jinn and Kenobi continued an investigation into Lundi's research of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] teachings, Kenobi noticed himself being affected by Lundi's anger and wondered if all Quermians had abilities of [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathy]] in the vein of Poof's skill with [[Mind trick/Legends|Force suggestion]].<ref name="TheFollowers">''[[Jedi Apprentice Special Edition: The Followers]]''</ref>

===The Yinchorri Uprising===
{{Quote|You seem troubled.''"<br />"''Getting old, perhaps I am&hellip; After so many years of relative peace, troubles me does a threat like this. Fly into danger, they do&hellip; But face uncertainty also do we who remain.|Yarael Poof and Yoda, regarding the mission to Yinchorr|<ref name="ActsOfWar1">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 1|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:RaidOnTheJediTempleJedi-ActsOfWar2.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Poof aids in the defense of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant.]]
In the years leading up to the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], Poof was the most senior of four Quermian Jedi within the Jedi Order.<ref name="FactFile100" /> In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]],<ref name="DarkHorseTimeline">{{DarkHorse|url=Zones/StarWars/Timeline|text=Comics Timeline}}</ref> Poof was present in the Jedi Council Chamber when the High Council received a distress signal sent from the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Mayvitch 7]] during the [[Battle of Mayvitch 7]], four [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after the battle took place. After deliberation over the capabilities of the aggressors, the [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]], the Council agreed to send Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] to the planet [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]] to [[Second mission to the Yinchorri system|investigate]]. Poof, alongside [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], observed as Windu departed alongside multiple Jedi volunteers. Later, Poof was present when Yoda received word that Windu's team had been attacked after exiting [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] in the [[Yinchorri system]].<ref name="ActsOfWar1" />

Soon thereafter, a strike team of Yinchorri began a [[Raid on the Jedi Temple (Yinchorri Uprising)|raid]] on the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. The Jedi in the temple, including Poof, ambushed the Yinchorri when they had barely entered. After successfully staving off the assault, Poof commented that the Yinchorri were more bloodthirsty than they had anticipated&mdash;upon which Yoda corrected him, affirming that the Yinchorri were simply misguided and were influenced by an [[Order of the Sith Lords|outside party]].<ref name="ActsOfWar2">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 2|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 2]]</ref> After Windu's team had been initially unsuccessful in locating the [[Yinchorri command center]] on three planets in the system, Yaddle informed Poof, alongside other members of the High Council, that she had discovered mention of another planet, [[Uhanayih]], in a [[Tharence Wo's holocron|holocron]] created by Jedi Master [[Tharence Wo]]. Shortly after the Council learned of Uhanayih, Windu contacted them from Yinchorr, informing them that he, too, had learned of the command center's location. Immediately afterward, the Jedi, including Poof, learned of Jedi Master [[Micah Giiett]]'s death after he had served on the team Jedi on Yinchorr.<ref name="ActsOfWar4">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 4|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 4]]</ref>

[[File:Micah_Giiett_JCAOW1.png|thumb|right|200px|Poof would learn of the death of fellow High Council member Micah Giiett (pictured).]]
Following the Yinchorri's surrender, Poof attended the return of Windu's team and watched as the corpses of those who perished on the mission were unloaded. Afterward, Poof convened with the High Council, which discussed the prospect of the Yinchorri being left at the behest of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] of the Republic, as well as the matter of filling the late Giiett's seat on the Council&mdash;which Windu proposed should be taken by Jedi Knight [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]].<ref name="ActsOfWar4" /> Shortly following the Yinchorri Uprising, Jinn and Kenobi apprehended the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Vilmarh Grahrk]] and brought him before the Jedi High Council&mdash;Poof included&mdash;to whom he confessed to hiring the Yinchorri, though he was unable to identify who had, in turn, hired him. Thus, the Council decided to release Grahrk, hoping he would lead them to his employer.<ref name="SW-1998-41">[[Star Wars (1998) 41|''Star Wars'' (1998) 41]]</ref> The [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] lamented his lack of involvement in the Yinchorri Uprising to his master and the orchestrator of the conflict, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Maul affirmed that he would have been able to kill far more Jedi in the conflict, including members of the Jedi Council.<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

===Protecting Valorum===
{{Quote|The Nebula Front is not the important concern here. It is the Trade Federation that matters.''"<br />"Thought ''to be less important, the Nebula Front is. But directing this, they are. Directing all of this.|Poof and Yoda|<ref name="CloakofDeception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref>}}
[[File:FinisValorum-FF56.png|thumb|left|250px|Poof and the Jedi Council set out to protect Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum (pictured).]]
At some point between 33 and [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="LostJediDate">{{DarkHorse|url=Zones/StarWars/Timeline|text=Comics Timeline}} dates the events of ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Council: Acts of War]]'', which include [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi's]] accession to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], to [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], while [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']] dates [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn's]] [[Death/Legends|death]] to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. ''[[Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi]]'' must take place between those [[Standard year/Legends|years]] as it shows Mundi being a member of the Council and Jinn being alive.</ref> Poof&mdash;alongside the rest of the High Council&mdash;tasked Jinn and two other Jedi&mdash;Knights [[Vel Ardox]] and [[Noro Zak]]&mdash;with [[Mission to Esseles|traveling]] to [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] and locating Jedi Master Adi Gallia. However, they also forbade him from bringing Kenobi along for the mission. Although Kenobi disobeyed the Council's orders for him to remain behind, Jinn's mission was ultimately successful.<ref name="LostJedi">''[[Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi]]''</ref>

In 32 BBY,<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Poof was among the members of the Jedi High Council who debriefed Jinn following the [[Attack on Supreme Chancellor Valorum|attempted assassination]] of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] of the Republic. The Council tasked Jinn, Kenobi, the Jedi Knight [[Vergere]], and four of its own members&mdash;Masters [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]], Ki-Adi-Mundi, [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]], and Yaddle&mdash;with further investigation. The Council, minus those four, later reconvened to discuss the [[Mission to Asmeru|mission]] Jinn's group had taken to the planet [[Asmeru/Legends|Asmeru]]. Despite concerns that the [[Nebula Front]] resistance group had taken the Jedi on Asmeru hostage, Poof maintained that the Council and Chancellor Valorum needed to focus on the Trade Federation's involvement. However, Yoda countered that the Nebula Front was orchestrating the entire incident. Poof later questioned if the [[Ancient Houses|Senex Houses]] would remain neutral in the conflict, to which Master [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]] suggested an accord with the Republic to ensure it would be so. After the incident resolved, the High Council reconvened once more. Poof questioned the motivation of the Nebula Front militants [[Arwen Cohl]] and "[[Eru Matalis|Havac]]" in orchestrating the recent events, and Windu surmised that it was to bring down Valorum and the Trade Federation.<ref name="CloakofDeception" />

===Naboo and the Chosen One===
{{Quote|He is to be trained, then?''"<br />"''No, he will not be trained.''"<br />"''No?''"<br />"''He is too old.''"<br />"''He ''is'' the chosen one. You must see it.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Mace Windu, regarding the Jedi Council's decision|<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />}}
[[File:YaraelPoof-FF100.png|thumb|right|200px|Poof (pictured) was among those on the Jedi High Council who ordered a probe into the Trade Federation.]]
In the weeks prior to the Battle of Naboo<ref name="ObiWan" /> in 32 BBY,<ref name="JVS" /> Poof was one member of the Jedi High Council that oversaw [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] between Kenobi and the [[Jedi training droid/Legends|Jedi training droid]] [[JTR-47]]. After Kenobi was assigned to look into the [[Black Heth]] street gang in the lower levels of Coruscant, Poof was present among the High Council as the Padawan and Jinn debriefed on the [[Skirmishes on Coruscant|skirmishes]] with the gang. After further investigation, Kenobi reported to the High Council once again with the information that the Black Heth were acting as a front for a group of [[Jin'ha]] arms dealers. Following the meeting, the Council decided to send Masters Plo Koon and [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]] to further [[First mission to Obredaan|investigate]] on<ref name="ObiWan">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref> the planet [[Obredaan]].<ref name="TEA" /> After the Council lost communication with Koon and Koth, they sent Kenobi and Jinn to Obredaan to [[Second mission to Obredaan|assist]]. When the Jedi Masters were freed and Kenobi discovered a [[Jin'ha cortosis mine|cortosis mine]] operated by the Jin'ha, the Council took the remainder of the investigation into their own hands.<ref name="ObiWan" />

In the same year,<ref name="ShadowHunterDate">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]'' to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> the Jedi Council had a meeting with Jedi Master [[Anoon Bondara]] and his Padawan, [[Darsha Assant]], where they assigned her a [[Mission to the Crimson Corridor|mission]] to the [[Crimson Corridor]] in Coruscant's [[Zi-Kree Sector]]. She was tasked by the Council with locating [[Oolth]], a former member of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime syndicate, who had information regarding a recent change in the power structure of the underworld. This task was to serve as her final trial as a Padawan. After the mission took a turn for the worse, Assant speculated that the Council would send a "real" Jedi to retrieve her following her failure. When Assant returned to the Jedi Temple and reported her failure to Bondara, the latter declined reporting to the Council, stating that they would only do so after confirming whether or not Oolth had died. When they returned to the scene of his apparent death, the Jedi Master finally conceded that they needed to report to the High Council&mdash;though their chance was cut short when they were [[Skirmish on Coruscant (32 BBY)|assailed]] by Maul, and Bondara sacrificed himself in a vain attempt to stop him. Having learned of an impending Trade Federation [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] from the informants [[Lorn Pavan]] and [[I-5YQ]], Assant resolved to deliver the duo to the Council to warn them of the plot. Before she could do so, she and the informants were likewise slain by the Sith apprentice. Further investigation of the incident from Kenobi only indicated involvement from Black Sun, which he wished to report to the Council.<ref name="ShadowHunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> The Council then, on behalf of Chancellor Valorum, deployed Jinn and Kenobi to Naboo to [[Mission to Naboo|negotiate]] with the Trade Federation regarding their blockade of the planet,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> as well as their potential collaboration with the Jin'ha.<ref name="ObiWan" />

[[File:High_Council_Chamber.png|thumb|left|300px|The Jedi High Council, including Poof, tests Anakin Skywalker.]]
Jinn and Kenobi were ambushed during their mission and forced to [[Capture of Theed/Legends|evacuate]] the [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen of Naboo]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], from the planet as the Trade Federation invaded. The group took brief refuge on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and, following a [[Duel on Tatooine/Legends|duel]] there between Maul and Jinn, returned to Coruscant. Jinn reported the events that had transpired to the Jedi High Council in the Jedi Council Chamber, as well as his belief that Maul was a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]. Additionally, he revealed to the High Council the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], whom he believed to be the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]]. The Council agreed to test the boy, but, after the test, decided against training him due to his age and temperament. Jinn was then re-assigned to continue assisting Queen Amidala in order to discern the identity of Maul&mdash;Skywalker's future was to be decided at a later time. After the Battle of Naboo where Jinn met his death, Kenobi was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight and given permission by the High Council to take Skywalker as his apprentice.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

===After Naboo===
{{Quote|Relations between the Jedi and the guardians have been ''strained'' since Tinte ''[sic]'' became Sheyf. With the possible re-emergence of the Sith, we must look for a way to better interactions.|Poof, regarding recent actions from Quinlan Vos|<ref name="SW1998Issue32">[[Star Wars (1998) 32|''Star Wars'' (1998) 32]]</ref>}}
Poof eventually reconvened with the Jedi High Council<ref name="SW1998Issue13">[[Star Wars (1998) 13|''Star Wars'' (1998) 13]]</ref>&mdash;again in 32 BBY<ref name="EmissariesDate">{{DarkHorse|url=Zones/StarWars/Timeline|text=Comics Timeline}} establishes that the events of ''[[Star Wars: Emissaries to Malastare]]'' take place in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The website also states that ''Emissaries to Malastare'' takes place following {{Film|I}}.</ref>&mdash;to discuss sending six emissaries from the Jedi Council to assist in the [[Lannik–Red Iaro peace negotiations]]. After selecting which of its members would attend the negotiations, the Council dispersed.<ref name="SW1998Issue13" /> In [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]], Poof was present among the High Council when they discussed the recent murders of Jedi Knight [[J'Mikel]] and Jedi Master [[Peerce]] at the hands of the former Jedi and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]]. After deliberation, the Council agreed to [[Hunt for Aurra Sing|send]] Adi Gallia, Ki-Adi-Mundi, and his Padawan [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]] after Sing.<ref name="SW1998Issue28">[[Star Wars (1998) 28|''Star Wars'' (1998) 28]]</ref>

That same year, Poof and other Jedi were contacted by [[Sheyf]] [[Tinté Vos]], requesting the aid of Jedi Knight [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]]&mdash;Tinté's great-nephew&mdash;in investigating a raid on a [[Kiffex security compound|security compound]] on the planet [[Kiffex/Legends|Kiffex]]. Alongside Quinlan, Poof, Tiin, and Windu received the message from Tinté. After instructing Quinlan to wait for their decision, Tiin and Poof objected to sending Quinlan on the basis that he seemed to be moving closer to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] and relations between the [[Kiffu Guardians]] and Jedi being already strained. After further deliberation, the Council nonetheless agreed to send Quinlan to Kiffex.<ref name="SW1998Issue32" />

[[File:SW41JediFightClub.png|thumb|right|250px|Vilmarh Grahrk described a falsified brawl between various Jedi High Council members in which Poof allegedly participated.]]
Later in 30 BBY, Grahrk told an embellished version of his capture and release at the hands of the Jedi Order following the Yinchorri Uprising to a group of patrons in the [[Cluster]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on<ref name="SW-1998-41" /> the moon [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="TEA" /> In his recounting of events, he claimed that his employer, "Bobo"&mdash;who was, in fact, Darth Sidious&mdash;had used the Yinchorri Uprising as a cover to steal the "[[Secret Treasure of the Jedi]]." He further claimed that this theft enraged the members of the High Council&mdash;Poof included&mdash;to the point they had begun brawling between one another until Grahrk allegedly offered to retrieve it for the Jedi, prompting their adoration. The smuggler further recounted that he had successfully recovered the treasure from "Bobo," bringing additional praise from Poof and the other High Council members.<ref name="SW-1998-41" /> Poof was later present as the High Council ascended Vos to the rank of Jedi Master and his Padawan, [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], to the rank of Jedi Knight.<ref name="SW-1998-45">[[Star Wars (1998) 45|''Star Wars'' (1998) 45]]</ref> In [[28 BBY/Legends|28 BBY]], Poof was among the councilors who elected to send Kenobi and Skywalker to act as protectors for [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Palpatine during a diplomatic mission with members of the [[Colicoid/Legends|Colicoid]] species.<ref name="JediQuest1">[[Jedi Quest 1|''Jedi Quest'' 1]]</ref>

===Hero of Coruscant===
{{Quote|&hellip; Perhaps ''I'' would be a better choice. My mental abilities are reasonably well honed ''[sic]''. They could prove to be advantageous in such an endeavor.|Yarael Poof, to Mace Windu|<ref name="ZamWesell">''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TheDeathofYaraelPoof.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Poof is stabbed by Ashaar Khorda.]]
In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]],<ref name="WesellDate" /> Windu revealed to the Council that an [[Annoo-dat Prime]] radical, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Ashaar Khorda]], was in possession of the [[Infant of Shaa]], an ancient artifact with enough power to split a planet into two. Poof said such a weapon would send ripples through the Force. Concurring, Yoda declared that the responsibility solving this crisis rested upon members of the Council itself. Windu initially announced his intent to investigate on Coruscant&mdash;one of three potential targets&mdash;but Poof interjected, proposing that his own skills were better honed to locate such a [[Disturbance in the Force/Legends|disturbance in the Force]]. After Windu relented, the Quermian Jedi Master set out on his task. During his search, Poof encountered a [[Unidentified child (Coruscant)|youngling]] being chased by a [[Spiz's gang|gang]] led by the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Spiz]]. Poof intervened, conjuring an illusion of a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] to scare the gang off. After explaining he had merely made the gang's fears more visible, he then explained to the youngling that he was a member of the High Council in search of a dangerous artifact and that he could sense it through the Force. After ensuring the youngling would be alright, Poof continued searching for the Infant of Shaa deeper into Coruscant's alleys.<ref name="ZamWesell" />

The Jedi Master eventually tracked the artifact to a [[Power relay/Legends|power relay]]. He warned Khorda and his lackeys to remain where they were to keep from being harmed. Just then, the bounty hunters [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] and [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] also entered the relay. Khorda ordered his lackeys to [[Skirmish at Coruscant's power core|attack]] the Jedi Master and bounty hunters, forcing Poof to brandish his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] in self-defense. He cut down his opponents as he made his way to Khorda and eventually disarmed the extremist before beginning to reach for the Infant of Shaa. Just before Poof was able to grab the artifact, however, Khorda retaliated, fatally stabbing him in the gut. Fett dispatched Khorda in response, causing the artifact to nearly fall until Wesell caught it. The bounty hunters then handed the Infant of Shaa back to Poof, who, using the remnants of his energy, bound the artifact's Force energies back into itself. With Coruscant saved from annihilation, Poof then died.<ref name="ZamWesell" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|I've seen too many of these, master. Is this what awaits me?''"<br />"''The pyre is the end for which all true Jedi are destined, Anakin Skywalker. Yes, the death of any of us is a sad thing. But Master Poof is one with the Force now.|Anakin Skywalker and Mace Windu, regarding Poof's funeral|<ref name="ZamWesell" />}}
[[File:ColemanTrebor-DB.png|thumb|right|250px|Yarael Poof was succeeded in his position on the Jedi High Council by Jedi Master Coleman Trebor (pictured).]]
Poof's sacrifice was honored with a [[Funeral of Yarael Poof|funeral]] in which he was [[Cremation/Legends|cremated]] in the Jedi Temple, with the remainder of the Jedi High Council, Kenobi, Skywalker,<ref name="ZamWesell" /> fellow Quermian Jedi Knights [[Loo Raelo]], [[Vinian Ska]], and [[Kindee Ya]],<ref name="QuermianKnights">{{FactFile|100|POO 1-2|Yarael Poof}} states that [[Yarael Poof/Legends|Yarael Poof]] was one of only four [[Quermian/Legends|Quermians]] enlisted in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. The other three Quermians in the Order are depicted in ''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]'', albeit unidentified. ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' identifies the three Quermian Jedi aside from Poof as the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Loo Raelo]], [[Vinian Ska]], and [[Kindee Ya]], meaning the three must have been the Quermian Jedi depicted in ''Zam Wesell''.</ref> and others in attendance. Windu recited a eulogy for Poof, commending his bravery and sacrifice as the epitome of what a Jedi was. Skywalker, meanwhile, questioned if a fate similar to Poof's awaited him. Windu reassured him that Poof met the end of a true Jedi, sad as it were. Windu and Kenobi then discussed if the danger had truly passed; the former was certain it had, though he reasoned that Poof was likely not the only hero of Coruscant.<ref name="ZamWesell" /> Fellow High Council member Even Piell had personally mourned Poof's death.<ref name="FF-2014-52">{{FactFile2014|52|PIE 5-8|Even Piell}}</ref>

At some point between 27 and [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Poof was succeeded on the Jedi High Council by Jedi Master [[Coleman Trebor/Legends|Coleman Trebor]],<ref name="Insider62">{{InsiderCite|62|Who's Who in the Jedi Order}}</ref> who was selected in particular due to his ability to communicate with various groups across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and resolve crises peacefully.<ref name="FactFile106Trebor">{{FactFile|106|TRE 1-2|Coleman Trebor}}</ref> In [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]],<ref name="MomentOfTruthDate">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Jedi Quest: The Moment of Truth]]'' to [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]].</ref> Kenobi recounted the deaths of Jinn and Poof to himself as he contemplated the recent losses the Jedi Order had faced.<ref name="MomentOfTruth">''[[Jedi Quest: The Moment of Truth]]''</ref> In [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]],<ref name="HostagePrincessDate">''[[Star Wars Adventures 3: The Hostage Princess]]'' is set four [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Yarael Poof. ''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]'', which include Poof's death, to [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], so ''The Hostage Princess'' must take place in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]].</ref > the absence of Poof still resonated among all Jedi. Windu and Jedi Master [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] attended a memorial for Poof on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], Quermia, that year. However, their visit was cut short by a call for aid from Kenobi, Skywalker, and Jedi Knight [[Bultar Swan/Legends|Bultar Swan]], who were undergoing a [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|mission]] to the planet [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]].<ref name="HostagePrincess">''[[Star Wars Adventures 3: The Hostage Princess]]''</ref>

Around [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Tionne Solusar]] recounted Poof's skills in creating illusions in her book ''[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force]]''. Solusar also shared the recording Poof had stored in Krimsan's [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] in her book.<ref name="JediVsSith" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I should be going. And you should hurry home. Will you be all right?|Yarael Poof, asking a youngling if they would be alright before continuing on his mission|<ref name="ZamWesell" />}}
[[File:Yarael_poofEGTTF.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Yarael Poof was a wise and compassionate Jedi Master.]]
Yarael Poof had an unusual appearance, with<ref name="CSWEYarael">{{CSWECite|III|37|Poof, Yarael}}</ref> [[Color|pasty white]] skin and red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="YaraelDB" /> Like other Quermians, he possessed two pairs of spindly [[Limb/Legends|arms]]&mdash;the second of which he hid beneath his [[Jedi apparel/Legends|robes]]&mdash;granting him improved dexterity, as well as a lower [[Brain/Legends|brain]] within his chest, olfactory glands in his hands, and a long neck supporting a bulbous<ref name="CSWEYarael" /> and small head.<ref name="MeetTheCouncil">''[[Meet the Jedi High Council]]''</ref> Alongside his long legs, Poof's neck gave him a height nearly three [[Foot/Legends|feet]] taller than other [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], standing at 2.64 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="FactFile100" /> or 8 feet and 8 inches.<ref name="SWCE" /> Poof used both of his brains during debates among the High Council.<ref name="MysteriesOfTheJedi">''[[Star Wars: Mysteries of the Jedi]]''</ref>

Poof was a wise Quermian whose connection with the Force was admired by all. He spoke very little during High Council meetings but was nonetheless respected for his insight. His extensive past experience made him prepared for field duty. Poof was soft-natured and preferred to avoid violent conflict;<ref name="FactFile100" /> this aversion to violence, in turn, led to his preference for illusory [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]].<ref name="PowerOfTheJedi" /> Poof was compassionate to the point that he was willing to help others even when actively undertaking another mission.<ref name="FactFile106Yarael">{{FactFile|106|POO 3-4|Yarael Poof}}</ref> After Poof's death, Windu described him as among the best of the Jedi Order and the epitome of what all Jedi strive to be.<ref name="ZamWesell" /> He had a mischievous side and enjoyed playing mind tricks on colleagues.<ref name="SWCE" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|But if a guard had seen me, I might make him believe I was nothing but a gust of wind, or the shadow of a soaring indigenous avian. A Jedi can do such things, for it is the will of the Force.|Yarael Poof|<ref name="JediVsSith" />}}
Poof was renowned as legendary for his mind trickery skills,<ref name="Scrapbook">''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Scrapbook]]''</ref> and his connection to the Force was admired by all.<ref name="FactFile100" /> Using those skills, he was capable of bringing conflicts to a quick end by turning the fears of his combatants against themselves,<ref name="TPMVD">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> sometimes through the conjuration of illusions of beasts and soldiers, which were refined through his skill with [[battle meditation]].<ref name="FactFile100" /> He could also give courage to his own forces while weakening the resolve of their enemies.<ref name="TENGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> A lesser-known ability of Poof's was [[combustion]].<ref name="TNEGC" /> Other Force abilities he could use included skills from the [[Alter (Jedi Order)|Alter]], [[Control]], and [[Sense]] branches of Jedi powers, such as [[Force empathy/Legends|Force empathy]], [[Enhance Attribute]], [[Magnify Senses]], [[Tutaminis]], [[Force stealth]], [[Force healing/Legends|Force healing]], [[Inspire]], [[Sense Force]], telepathy, and [[Force-bond/Legends|Force Mind]]. Poof could also strike others through the Force by means of [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]]. The Jedi Master had some skill in deflection and blocking of attacks, as well as with [[Computer/Legends|computers]], diplomacy, and intimidation. He had some knowledge of Jedi lore. Alongside [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], Poof was able to read, speak, and write in [[Quermian (language)/Legends|Quermian]], and he could also speak [[Mon Calamari (language)|Mon Calamarian]], [[Cerean (language)|Cerean]], and [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]].<ref name="PowerOfTheJedi" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Look! He is ''Jedi!''|One of Ashaar Khorda's lackeys, upon spotting Yarael Poof's lightsaber|<ref name="ZamWesell" />}}
Poof wore a set of brown [[Robe/Legends|robes]], under which he concealed his second pair of arms and on top of which he was also adorned with a [[Cannom collar/Legends|cannom collar]] in line with the traditions of his species.<ref name="SWCE" /> He also carried a blue lightsaber of his own.<ref name="ZamWesell" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
{{Quote|If you think back to the original Jedi Council there was a long-necked Jedi on the far side&mdash;Yarael Poof&mdash;he was a puppet. George was afraid that if we kept that guy in, people might confuse him with the Kaminoans.|''Attack of the Clones'' animation director [[Rob Coleman]], regarding Yarael Poof|<ref name="Homing Beacon #67">{{HBCite|67}}</ref>}}
[[File:YaraelPoofConcept.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Early concept art of Yarael Poof, which was labeled simply "Alien Jedi"]]
Yarael Poof was first shown in the teaser trailer for the [[May]] [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]].<ref name="TPMTeaser">{{SW|url=video/episode-i-teaser-trailer|text=Episode I Teaser Trailer}}</ref> The trailer debuted in theaters across twenty-six cities on [[November 17]], [[1998]],<ref name="SWYBY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> with a wider release on [[November 20]] that year.<ref name="TPMTeaser" /> He was first identified on [[April 21]], 1999,<ref name="PocketGuideDate">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Episode-Whos-Who/dp/0762405198|text=Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide To The Characters In The Phantom Menace}}</ref> in the reference book [[Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide to the Characters of The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'' Episode I ''Who's Who: A Pocket Guide to the Characters of The Phantom Menace'']], written by [[Ryder Windham]].<ref name="PocketGuide">''[[Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide to the Characters of The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> His first appearance was a storybook adaptation of ''The Phantom Menace'', [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook'']],<ref name="Storybook">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook'']]</ref> which was released in [[April]] 1999 and published by [[Random House]].<ref name="StorybookDate">{{RandomHouseOld|url=kids/catalog/display.pperl?isbn=0375800255|text=Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook}}</ref>

In ''The Phantom Menace'', Poof was portrayed by a puppet operated by [[Michelle Taylor]].<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> Filming for ''The Phantom Menace'' took place from [[June 26]], [[1997]] to [[September 30]] that year,<ref name="SW-Fully Operational Fandom: Visiting Star Wars Filming Locations">{{SW|url=news/fully-operational-fandom-visiting-star-wars-filming-locations|text=Fully Operational Fandom: Visiting ''Star Wars'' Filming Locations}}</ref> with the scenes involving the Jedi High Council&mdash;including Yarael Poof&mdash;having taken place during the third phase of principal photography at [[Leavesden Studios]]<ref name="Insider66">{{InsiderCite|66|Star Wars Q&A|''Star Wars'' Q&A}}</ref> in [[Wikipedia:Watford|Watford]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]].<ref name="Leavesden">{{WebCite|url=https://www.wbsl.com/studios/about/find-us|text=Find Us - The Studios|date=2025|work=Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden|archivedate=20250603011208}}</ref> The puppet for Poof was built directly into his chair inside the set for the Jedi Council Chamber,<ref name="Insider66" /> with Taylor<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> inside the puppet controlling his appendages and neck.<ref name="Insider66" />

Poof was originally slated to reappear in the second installment of the ''Star Wars'' prequel trilogy, the film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]&mdash;released on [[May 16]], [[2002]]<ref name="AotCDate">{{ThisWeek|u0Z7i0LnXOg|Mandalorian Season 2 Directors, We Celebrate a Birthday, and More!|sw_url=video/mandalorian-season-2-directors-we-celebrate-a-birthday-and-more}}</ref>&mdash;but ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] was concerned that viewers would confuse him with the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]], a new species introduced in the film. As no new footage of the Jedi Council chambers was shot for Episode II, archive footage from Episode I was reused. In order to remove him from the film, Poof was digitally painted out of the footage and replaced by Coleman Trebor, a new Jedi Master designed for the movie.<ref name="Homing Beacon #67" /> Released on [[April 22]], 2002,<ref name="AotCIllustratedDate">{{Amazon|domain=co.uk|url=Star-Wars-Attack-Clones-Illustrated/dp/0091884780|text=Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Illustrated Companion}}</ref> the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Illustrated Companion]]'', written by [[Marcus Hearn]], misspells Poof's first name as "Yareal,"<ref name="AotCCompanion">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Illustrated Companion]]''</ref> as does the [[2006]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', written by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]] and [[Helen Keier]].<ref name="TENGAS" /> The [[2011]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'', written by [[Simon Beecroft]], erroneously states that Poof was a member of the High Council during the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="SWCE" /> despite his death having occurred five years prior.<ref name="Anachronisms">Yarael Poof's death is depicted in ''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]'', which ''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' dates to [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]]. Meanwhile, ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of the [[Clone Wars]] to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], and the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]] to 19 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]] onwards. As such, any depiction of Yarael Poof during these eras is anachronistic in nature.</ref>

===Non-canon history===
====''Robot Chicken''====
=====Council underdog=====
{{Quote|Who can't use the Force now? I can still use the Force. Let's put that one to a vote, because I don't even know what that means. Does anyone realize that I'm talking?|Yarael Poof|<ref name="RobotChickenIII">''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode III]]''</ref>}}
[[File:YaraelRobotChicken.png|thumb|left|250px|Yarael Poof in ''Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode III'']]
Yarael Poof appears in multiple skits in the [[2010]] comedy special ''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode III]]'', voiced by [[Dan Milano]]. In the first sketch, which takes place during the events of ''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'', Poof is seated among the Jedi High Council as they discuss the matter of training Anakin Skywalker. Yoda initially states that the boy should not be trained due to the darkness inside of him, only for Mace Windu to point out that he could bring balance to the Force and for Yoda to agree. Poof interjects, reminding Yoda that he had just claimed training Skywalker would be a bad thing. When Yoda mentions the prophecy of the Chosen One, Poof questions what exactly the prophecy is and why he is unaware of it. Windu ignores him, stating that he will inform Skywalker of the Council's decision the following day. The Quermian Jedi Master once again interjects, sarcastically remarking that they are apparently now a council rather than solely Yoda and Windu and asking a member he referred to as "Dogface" if they are also aware of this "revelation."<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />

Once again, Yoda and Windu ignore Poof, declaring they need to inform the Senate of their lessened ability to use the Force. Poof responds by stating that he can still use the Force and that they should put the claim to a vote, then ponders if his remarks are actually being listened to. After a brief pause, Windu announces that the Council should stop for the day to eat. Yoda then suggests that Poof pick up [[Pizza/Legends|pizza]], to which the entire council&mdash;excluding Poof himself&mdash;agree. Poof complains that he had just picked up their [[coffee]] the day prior and has yet to be reimbursed despite submitting the receipt, but he then sarcastically says he would still pick up their food if it was the will of the Council. He then informs Yaddle that he needs to borrow her [[Groundcar/Legends|car]], prompting her to lie that it was in the shop. Poof states he had just seen it downstairs in the Jedi Temple, to which she responded with a new excuse of "insurance." Poof exasperatedly then declares he is going anyway, remarking that despite being one of twelve Jedi in the entire galaxy on the Jedi High Council, today it was his job to retrieve the pizza. He then sarcastically remarks that his parents are very proud.<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />

=====Order 66=====
{{Quote|They didn't have calamari pizza because Mon Calamari are people, and I did not know that.|Yarael Poof|<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />}}
[[File:YaraelPizza.png|thumb|right|250px|Yarael Poof carries pizza.]]
The second sketch takes place during the events of the<ref name="RobotChickenIII" /> [[2005]] film&mdash;and third installment of the ''Star Wars'' prequel trilogy<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref>&mdash;[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />&mdash;and thus anachronistically due to Poof's death prior to the Clone Wars<ref name="Anachronisms" />&mdash;and narratively follows the first sketch. Poof returns to the High Council's chamber during [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] carrying a stack of pizza boxes, announcing that he could not get [[calamari pizza]] due to the Mon Calamari's status as a people, something he was unaware of. After stating this, Poof realizes the Council chamber is in ruins and that everyone on the Council may be dead. Declaring his time is short, he sets the pizza boxes down and runs to a seat in the chamber. Once seated, he begins mocking Yoda, making fun of his manner of speech and complaining once again that he never allowed the other Council members to talk. Shortly afterwards, an explosion occurs outside the temple, prompting Poof to panic and leave&mdash;though he collects the pizza boxes again as he does so.<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />

=====Imperial chef=====
{{Quote|Everyone I know is dead.|Yarael Poof|<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />}}
[[File:YaraelInHiding.png|thumb|left|150px|Yarael Poof in hiding.]]
The third sketch depicts Poof<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />&mdash;once again anachronistically<ref name="Anachronisms" />&mdash;during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]]. Poof is working, disguised with a fake mustache, as a chef under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. While working, he is approached by Darth Vader and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine, the former of who requests bisque for his meal. Poof panics and drops his ladle, prompting Palpatine to request cream of spinach, albeit with a different ladle. Poof nervously hands the two Sith Lords their meals and they walk away. Shortly thereafter, Palpatine senses a "disturbance" in the Force, and the pair return to Poof, who is still panicking. Palpatine then states the Quermian had forgotten to give them crackers, which he then provides. After the Sith Lords walk away once again, Poof distressingly comments that everyone he knows is dead.<ref name="RobotChickenIII" />

====''The Padawan Menace''====
{{Quote|Tracked the battle droid to Hoth, I have. Pursue him, I will.|Yoda, to the Jedi High Council|<ref name="PadawanMenace">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]]''</ref>}}
[[File:LEGOPoof-PadawanMenace.png|thumb|right|250px|Yoda speaks to Poof and the rest of the Jedi Council from Hoth.]]
Poof anachronistically<ref name="Anachronisms" /> appears in the 2011 [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] television special ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]]''. During the Clone Wars, Grand Master Yoda and the Padawan-impersonator "[[Han Solo/Legends|Ian]]" chase a [[Unidentified B1 battle droid (Asajj Ventress)|B1-series battle droid]] carrying plans for a Separatist attack on Coruscant to the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. When there, Yoda contacts the Jedi High Council, including Yarael Poof, informing them of his progress. Ian then interrupts the holo-transmission, changing its "channel" to various shows including ''[[Ackbar Tonight]]'', ''[[Keeping up with the Calrissians]]'', infomercials, and a [[Music/Legends|singing]] competition. All the while, Poof observes and is startled by the sudden changes. Later, when Ian and the other Padawans are rewarded for their bravery on Coruscant, Poof is in the crowd celebrating.<ref name="PadawanMenace" />
